sections.shortTitle: Balochistan Essential Health Services Code of Conduct Ordinance 2011
sections.description:
Short title, application and commencement

ORDINANCE II OF 2011
ORDINANCE II OF 2011
BALOCHISTAN ESSENTIAL HEALTH SERVICES (CODE Of CONDUCT) ORDINANCE, 2011
An Ordinance to make provisions
for better regulation of Health Services in Balochistan and the matters
connected therewith or incidental thereto
[Gazette of Balochistan, Extraordinary, 18th June, 2011]
Legis:2-20/Law/2011,
dated 18-6-2011.---The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Balochistan
on 17th June, 2011 is hereby published for general information.
Preamble.--Whereas it is necessary to make provisions for
the different cadres of Health Services such as to establish a professional,
efficient, effective, accountable and disciplined service for ensuring the
maintenance of Health Care and for mobilization in the event of any exigency as
well as the situation caused due to any natural disaster, it is expedient to
provide for regulation of the Balochistan Essential Health Service and for the
matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto;
And whereas the
Provincial assembly of Balochistan is not in session and the Governor is satisfied
that circumstances, exist which render it necessary to take immediately action;
Now, therefore, in
exercise of the powers conferred by Article 128(1) of the Constitution of
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, the Governor is pleased to make and
promulgate the following Ordinance:--
CHAPER-1
PRELIMINARY
1. Short title,
application and commencement.--(1)
This Ordinance may be called the Balochistan Essential Health Services (Code of
Conduct) ,Ordinance, 2011.
(2) It shall apply
to all members of Health Services wherever they may be serving in Balochistan.
(3) It shall come
into force at once.

2. Definitions.--In this Ordinance, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context
(a)
"Code" means the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898 (Act V of 1898);
(b)
"Cognizable Offence" means an offence as defined in Criminal
Procedure Code, 1898 (Act V of 1898);
(c)
"Court" means the court of an Executive Magistrate First Class under
the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898 (Act V of 1898) or such other court to whom the
District Magistrate may transfer the case for trial;
(d) "Exigency
of Service", means in relation to posting and transfer an urgent or
unforeseen situation which, for the reason to be recorded in writing
requires premature transfer of a member of Health Services for performance of
specific tasks or duties but not as a replacement for what should be rightly
treated as an efficiency and discipline matter;
(e)"Financial
Remunerations" means all Financial liabilities to which a
Government Servant is entitled after retirement on superannuation period or
qualifying service. It includes General Provident Fund, 'Commutation,
Gratuity, Pension and Group Insurance etc;
(f) "Member of
Health Services" means all officials and officers appointed in Health
department irrespective of grade, designation and place of posting. It inter
alia, includes Doctors of all cadres, Paramedics, Nurses, Lady Health Visitors,
Lady Health Workers, Pharmacists, Drug Inspectors and Ministerial Staff etc. of
Health establishment;.
(g) "Ordinance"
means the Balochistan Essential Health Services (Code of Conduct) Ordinance,
2011;
(h) "Private
Practice" means delivery of Health Care Services in lieu of remuneration
at private clinics or places other than Government Hospitals or those notified
by Government from time to time;
(i)
"Rules" means rules made under this Ordinance; and
(j)
"Schedule" means schedule to this Ordinance.

4. Ban on
strike.---(1) Notwithstanding
anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no member of
health services shall be allowed to go or attempt to go, call or attempt to
call, participate or attempt to participate, instigate or attempt to instigate
and observe or attempt to observe a strike or demonstration for whatsoever
reasons.
(2) Any member-of
health services found guilty of going or attempting to go, calling or
attempting to call, participating or attempting to participate, instigating or
attempting to instigate and observing or attempting to observe a strike or
demonstration for whatsoever reasons, shall be liable to be dismissed from
service.
sections.punishment:
shall be liable to be dismissed from
service.

6. Resignations
as protest during strike.---(1) In
the course of strike or demonstration, the resignations wilfully tendered by
members of health services before Chief Minister Balochistan, Chief Secretary
Balochistan, Minister Health Balochistan, Secretary Health Balochistan or
representatives of Media shall forthwith be deemed to have accorded assent of
the Competent Authority in which case dismissal orders shall be issued.
(2) Any resignation
so tendered and the dismissal orders issued thereupon shall not be liable to be
withdrawn.

Disqualification for private practice and punishment thereof.---(1) Any member of health services having been
dismissed from service under this chapter shall forthwith seize to continue

been dismissed from health services under this chapter, continuing to deliver
private practice shall be liable for conviction with a punishment of

9. Forfeiture of

Every member of health services so dismissed in contravention of sections 3, 4,

(a) be liable to

(b) have to refund

(2) All the above

10. Appointment
of members of health services on contract basis during strike/demonstration.---(1) Notwithstanding anything containedin any
other law for the time being in force, in the event of any such strike or
demonstration mentioned under the preceding sections it shall be lawful for the
Government to appoint, subject to rules, members of health services on contract
basis without the recommendations of the Balochistan Public Service Commissions
or the Departmental Selection Committee as the case may be.
(2) Every member of
health services so appointed shall, on appointment---
(a) be liable to
the same duties and responsibilities and be subject to the same authorities and
this Ordinance as a regular member of health services; and
(b) be subject to
the orders of Health Department.

14. Indemnity
and bar of jurisdiction.---(1) No
suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for
anything in good faith done or intended to be done under this Ordinance or any
rule made thereunder.
No court shall call
in question or permit to be called in question, anything done or any action
taken under this Ordinance or any rule made thereunder.
No court shall
grant any injunction or make any order, nor shall any court entertain any
proceedings, in relation to anything done or intended to be done or any action
taken or intended to be taken under this Ordinance or any rule made thereunder.

ORDINANCE II OF 2011
ORDINANCE II OF 2011
BALOCHISTAN ESSENTIAL HEALTH SERVICES (CODE Of CONDUCT) ORDINANCE, 2011
An Ordinance to make provisions
for better regulation of Health Services in Balochistan and the matters
connected therewith or incidental thereto
[Gazette of Balochistan, Extraordinary, 18th June, 2011]
Legis:2-20/Law/2011,
dated 18-6-2011.---The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Balochistan
on 17th June, 2011 is hereby published for general information.
Preamble.--Whereas it is necessary to make provisions for
the different cadres of Health Services such as to establish a professional,
efficient, effective, accountable and disciplined service for ensuring the
maintenance of Health Care and for mobilization in the event of any exigency as
well as the situation caused due to any natural disaster, it is expedient to
provide for regulation of the Balochistan Essential Health Service and for the
matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto;
And whereas the
Provincial assembly of Balochistan is not in session and the Governor is satisfied
that circumstances, exist which render it necessary to take immediately action;
Now, therefore, in
exercise of the powers conferred by Article 128(1) of the Constitution of
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, the Governor is pleased to make and
promulgate the following Ordinance:--
CHAPTER-III
RULE, DELEGATION OF POWERS AND INDEMNITY
16. Rule
making.--(1) The Government may by
a notification in the official gazette, make rules for carrying into effect the
provisions and purpose of this Ordinance.
(2) Every Rule or
regulation under this Ordinance shall be made by notification in the official
Gazette.

17. Delegation
of powers.---(1) In order to give
effect to the provisions of this Ordinance, Government may, by a notification in
the official Gazette, delegate all or any of its powers under this Ordinance to the
Provincial Health Department or an authority subordinate to it.
(2) The Provincial
Health Department may delegate all or any of its powers under this Ordinance to
an authority subordinate to it.
